0.original: <hex:024804F201FC03><hex:024904F201FD03> Quest Sync<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103><hex:02100103>Toffwyb seems excited to meet a real-life adventurer.

48.original: Are you... Are you one of those adventuring types I've heard so much about!? Oh, but this is perfect! I just happen to have an errand of the kind that adventurers love! Or so I'm told.

49.original: I'm holding on to some volumes my customers ordered in, but instead of coming to pick them up, they've all decided that they want their goods delivered. So, I find myself in need of a delivery drudge...er, person. Might that person be you!?

50.original: Huzzah! Let me give you the details, then. All in all, there are three books on the delivery docket.

51.original: The first, <hex:021A020203>Ishgardian Astrology: A Comprehensive Theory<hex:021A020103>, should be handed to the servant at Albright Manor. <hex:021A020203>The White Yonder<hex:021A020103> is for a certain talkative booklover who you'll know by the constant stream of chatter. And the last, <hex:021A020203>Narrow Road through the Deep Grass<hex:021A020103>, goes to one of the toughest, most unflappable gleaners I have ever met.

52.original: I'll just mark their locations on this handy map...like so. The books are bought and paid for─no need to collect any coin─but do return to me for your own reward!

53.original: If you just throw the books in the harbor, I <hex:021A020203>will<hex:021A020103> find out. Not that I think you would! ...I'm watching you.

54.original: Welcome to Albright Manor! ...Do you have an appointment?

55.original: Ah, yes, one copy of <hex:021A020203>Ishgardian Astrology: A Comprehensive Theory<hex:021A020103>, just as his lordship requested.

56.original: I must confess to some confusion, however... What interest would his lordship, an esteemed practitioner of Sharlayan astrology, have in such an outdated Ishgardian discipline?

57.original: ...Not that I am in any position to question his lordship's reading habits, of course. Ahem. On your way, then.

58.original: Please tell me you've brought my new book! I've been waiting for what feels like <hex:021A020203>ages<hex:021A020103> for the latest shipment to arrive!

59.original: Yes! Finally! Did you know <hex:021A020203>The White Yonder<hex:021A020103> was written by a lad of fourteen years? I myself questioned how reliable such a work could possibly be, but a Far Eastern colleague with whom I've been exchanging correspondence says he absolutely swears by it.

60.original: It describes the wonders of the Abalathian Sea of Clouds in exquisite detail, and is, by all accounts, a roaring good read. The bit about the fighting paissas is said to be an especially entertaining episode.

61.original: Well, I should let you return to your deliveries and whatnot. Thank you kindly for putting this long-awaited treat into my ever-so-grateful hands!

63.original: Ah, is that my book? Good. I need it for my journey.

64.original: I usually don't have a great deal of time for reading, but as I'm leaving for Othard on requisition duty, I wanted to do some research on Far Eastern cultures. I know little of the peoples of the Azim Steppe...

65.original: Hm... It says here that “there are fifty-one distinct Xaela tribes, each with their own customs and traditions. The Buduga, for example, are exclusively male, and are known for kidnapping male outsiders to replenish lost numbers...”

66.original: Is...is this accurate!? I'll need to tread carefully, it seems. Thank you for the timely delivery.

67.original: All safely delivered? Hah! Of course they were!

68.original: My shop is well known for carrying publications not only from Sharlayan authors, but from all manner of foreign chroniclers and tale-tellers. Meaning every time a new shipment comes in, I'm faced with an avalanche of work.

69.original: I would've been buried alive without your assistance today, so here's a little something to show my gratitude. Go on, you've earned it!
